root_cause.text: The SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag in skb_shinfo()->flags is not propagated when fragment descriptors are moved between skbs by various frag-transfer helpers, causing the destination skb to hold references to shared pages while falsely reporting no shared frags, which allows in-place writers like ESP input to modify read-only page-cache pages.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states that __pskb_copy_fclone() and skb_shift() fail to propagate the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG bit, and that this lets an unprivileged user write into the page cache of a root-owned read-only file via authencesn-ESN stray writes. The patch adds propagation of SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG in multiple functions (__pskb_copy_fclone, skb_shift, skb_gro_receive, skb_gro_receive_list, tcp_clone_payload, skb_segment) to fix the omission.

The patch adds propagation of SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG in multiple functions (__pskb_copy_fclone, skb_shift, skb_gro_receive, skb_gro_receive_list, tcp_clone_payload, skb_segment) to fix the omission.

candidates.rationale: When merging fragments into p, data_len is updated but SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag is not propagated from the source skb to p.
Truesize updated without propagating the shared frag flag.
Length updated without propagating shared frag flag.
Sets the number of fragments in destination skb without copying the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from source.
Increments reference count on fragment, indicating sharing, but does not set the SHARED_FRAG flag on the destination skb.

vuln_statements.explanation: Increments the reference count on a fragment being moved to the destination skb, indicating that the page is now shared, but fails to set the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag on the destination skb's shinfo->flags, leaving a false 'no shared frags' state.

Assigns the number of fragments in the destination skb without copying the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the source skb. If the source had shared fragments, the destination must inherit this flag to correctly reflect that pages are shared.
Updates the data length of the destination skb during fragment merge without propagating the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the source skb, which can lead to incorrect tracking of shared pages.
Updates the truesize of the destination skb during fragment merge without propagating the shared frag flag, missing the opportunity to set SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when pages are shared.
Updates the length of the destination skb during fragment merge without ensuring the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag is set, which could allow in-place writers to modify pages that are actually shared.
During GRO coalesce, updates the destination skb's truesize without propagating the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag from the source skb, allowing shared pages to go undetected.
During GRO coalesce, updates the length without copying the SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG flag, leading to a situation where the destination skb may reference shared pages but report no shared frags.
